description: Executable form of ak.vector.view.terminal_state_patch.v1. The vector was description-only: it asserted that the terminal patch MUST be accepted and that an actor-supplied state_changed_at MUST be rejected, and nothing ran. The acceptance half was the load-bearing one -- the registry consumer that flattened every object reducer-managed path set into one collection made that patch unregisterable, so the only protocol-level removal path for a shared View could not be written down at all. cases[] is the schema face: every instance is validated against the live schema. admission_cases[] is the behavioral face: the outcomes schema validation cannot express, each carrying the registered error and reason code it MUST fail with.

author_writable_partition.note: author_writable is not a third enumeration. It is the complement the reducer-managed path registry already fixes: every member view.schema.json declares, minus the effective forbidden set solved FOR THIS OBJECT, with state subtracted by the single registered universal exemption. The lint recomputes both halves from the live registry and fails on drift, so this fixture cannot become a stale second source.

cases.name: terminal_state_patch_is_accepted
cases.why: models/views.md section 3.1: a shared View has no tombstone event kind, so its protocol-level removal IS this patch. If this payload did not validate, the spec would have no removal path. The patch map key IS the path: the removal patch is {"state": "tombstoned"}, never a {"set": {...}} wrapper -- that wrapper is a legal path named `set`, which is not one of the registered allowed_paths and is not a member view.schema.json declares.

cases.name: terminal_state_patch_in_explicit_op_form_is_accepted
cases.why: patch.schema.json admits both the direct value form and the explicit $op object form for the same path. Both spellings of the removal patch MUST validate, or the removal path would depend on which form the producer happened to choose.

cases.name: terminal_state_patch_with_prestate_guard_is_accepted
cases.why: expected_state_digest names the single committed current value the patch was authored against; it is optional, and supplying it does not change the shape.

cases.name: update_payload_refuses_a_reducer_derived_member
cases.why: state_changed_at is produced by object_state_transition_time on the accepted transition. The closed payload has no member for it at all, which is the only shape that cannot be argued with.

cases.name: update_payload_refuses_an_object_snapshot
cases.why: Before the three kinds were split, one shared payload with an unguarded anyOf admitted every shape on every kind, so an update could carry a whole definition object.

cases.name: update_payload_requires_the_subject
cases.why: view_id is the typed current result subject; without it the write cannot be addressed.

cases.name: create_payload_accepts_the_author_definition
cases.why: payload.object is view.schema.json#/$defs/view_definition -- the same closed authoring region reconcile replaces.

cases.name: create_payload_refuses_a_self_reported_creator
cases.why: created_by is create-locked and produced by object_create_actor. The earlier payload declared it and asked semantic validation to cross-check it against the envelope; every later write retained the author-supplied value verbatim, so a forged creator became permanent truth.

cases.name: create_payload_refuses_a_self_reported_realm
cases.why: realm_id is produced by object_realm_binding from the stream that accepted the Event, never from the payload.

cases.name: create_payload_refuses_a_self_reported_state
cases.why: state is produced by object_initial_state. Pinning const active in the payload still made the author the nominal source of a member the reducer owns, and state is in universal_forbidden_patch_paths precisely so no author can reach it.

cases.name: create_payload_refuses_the_derived_id
cases.why: The View id is the create Event own event_id retyped; a payload id is a second, forgeable source.

cases.name: create_payload_refuses_a_patch
cases.why: Cross-kind shapes are refused at schema level, not by a runtime convention.

cases.name: reconcile_payload_accepts_the_author_definition
cases.why: reconcile replaces the definition wholesale and MUST address its subject.

cases.name: reconcile_definition_cannot_resurrect_or_tombstone
cases.why: state is a retained_member of the reconcile write, so reconcile can neither tombstone nor resurrect. The author region does not declare it.

cases.name: materialized_active_view_validates
cases.why: The result of composing the author definition with the create-lock and update derivations.

cases.name: materialized_terminal_view_validates
cases.why: After the accepted terminal patch: state_changed_at is present because the transition happened, and views.md section 3.1 requires it exactly then. One accepted Event produces both members, so common-fields.md section 3 pins the ordering created_at <= state_changed_at <= updated_at -- JSON Schema cannot express it, so the lint checks it on every materialized case instead.

cases.name: materialized_value_refuses_the_self_reportable_id
cases.why: The reader derives the id from the subject; storing it would leave two value shapes in one family.

admission_cases.name: legal_active_to_tombstoned_is_admitted
admission_cases.why: The half a rejection-only fixture silently drops. views.md section 3.1 gives a shared View no tombstone Event kind, so this admission IS the protocol-level removal path, and state_changed_at MUST be written from the accepted update's canonical lifecycle timestamp.

admission_cases.name: author_supplied_state_changed_at_is_refused
admission_cases.why: The rejection half the vector names. state_changed_at is in the effective forbidden set of the view object and is NOT one of the 13 registered allowed_paths, so the patch path itself is refused -- the author cannot backdate a lifecycle fact by writing it beside the transition.

admission_cases.name: unsetting_state_is_refused
admission_cases.why: The single registered universal_exemptions row hands ak.view.update the state PATH, not the right to delete the member: state is required by view.schema.json, so the composed post-state would not validate against the family's value schema. An unset that removed a View's lifecycle state would produce a third kind of absence -- neither active nor tombstoned -- that no reader can interpret.

admission_cases.name: an_unregistered_lifecycle_state_is_refused
admission_cases.why: state is a closed enum. The exemption opens one path, not an open lifecycle vocabulary.

admission_cases.name: an_update_of_a_view_that_was_never_created_is_refused
admission_cases.why: models/views.md section 3.2 bullet 1: the patch MUST NOT be applied to an implicit null or empty object, and the typed-current contract forbids filling that hole with a registered initial_value -- a base value may come only from a registered create or genesis write. event-and-patch.md section 4.3.1 names the code: a pre-state that cannot be uniquely bound is schema_violation with reason_code=reducer_projection_failed.

admission_cases.name: a_reconcile_of_a_view_that_was_never_created_is_refused
admission_cases.why: reconcile is a whole-value set, which makes it the tempting place to allow implicit creation. It MUST NOT: its registered retained_members[] read schema, realm_id, state, created_by and created_at off a frozen pre-state that does not exist here, so admitting it would have to invent create-locked truth.

admission_cases.name: turning_a_shared_view_private_is_refused
admission_cases.why: visibility IS author-writable -- it is one of the 13 allowed_paths -- so this rejection cannot come from the patch surface. It is the separate normative rule of views.md section 3.1: a private View lives as encrypted holder account data under ak.views.private.<view_id> and MUST NOT enter the shared reducer, so title, query and layout MUST NOT be left behind in the shared typed current result.

admission_cases.name: an_update_after_the_terminal_transition_is_refused
admission_cases.why: tombstoned is terminal. Without this, the removal path of section 3.1 would be reversible by an ordinary edit.

admission_cases.name: resurrecting_a_terminal_view_is_refused
admission_cases.why: The exemption that makes the tombstone patch registrable is the same path that would express a resurrection. The terminal gate, not the patch surface, is what separates them.

admission_cases.name: a_late_reconcile_does_not_bypass_the_terminal_gate
admission_cases.why: views.md section 3.2: a late or concurrent known-good definition MUST NOT bypass an accepted terminal fact. reconcile retains state rather than writing it, so without this gate the admission would leave a tombstoned View carrying a freshly republished definition.

admission_cases.name: a_stale_prestate_guard_fails_without_selecting_a_historical_candidate
admission_cases.why: DIGEST_B may well equal an older accepted value of this same View. That is exactly the resolution the guard forbids: the current value is the last accepted write at the position this write is applied, per its own stream's order, and there is no parallel branch to choose among. current-results.md gives the code -- a pre-state that is not field-for-field equal returns failed_precondition -- and no reason code is registered because the generic code already says precisely what failed.

admission_cases.name: an_exact_retry_of_an_accepted_update_produces_no_second_effect
admission_cases.why: Replay of the SAME Event identity, not a second Event with the same content. It returns the stored outcome and MUST NOT write again -- otherwise the terminal transition would move state_changed_at forward every time a retry crossed the wire. A second, differently identified Event carrying the same patch is NOT this case: it meets the terminal gate above.

admission_cases.name: a_patch_that_mixes_a_legal_and_an_illegal_path_stores_nothing
admission_cases.why: event-and-patch.md section 4.3.1: every path in one payload.patch map is a single atomic write. The legal title MUST NOT survive the refusal of the create-locked created_by, or an author would gain a way to land edits by attaching them to a doomed path.

admission_cases.name: the_three_kinds_advance_one_revision_of_one_result

given.note: sequence: ak.view.create, then ak.view.reconcile, then this update

admission_cases.why: views.md section 3.2: the three kinds write the SAME typed current result family. If they held three authority chains, ak.view.update's apply_patch would land on a result nothing had ever written -- and the typed-current contract forbids papering over that with a registered initial_value.
